content: If you miss a dose of your medication, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time of your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and proceed with your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to make up for the missed one. Store this medication in its original container at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Avoid storing it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information was last updated in May 2024. It is important to note that this document provides a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific situation. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your individual health needs. This medication is used to treat chronic hepatitis B, a viral infection of the liver. It works by slowing the growth of the virus, thereby reducing the amount of virus in your body. Before starting this medication, read the patient information leaflet provided by your pharmacist. Take the medication by mouth, with or without food, as directed by your doctor, usually once daily. Use it consistently to achieve the best results. To help you remember, take it at the same time each day. Do not increase, decrease, or stop the medication without consulting your doctor or pharmacist. Treatment with this medication alone is not suitable for patients who are co-infected with both hepatitis B and HIV. Worsening of your condition, reduced response to treatment, or infection with resistant virus strains may occur during or after treatment. Common side effects may include weakness, headache, fever, increased cough, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or gas. Remember that your doctor has prescribed this medication because they believe the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for guidance. Before taking this medication, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. It is unknown if this medication passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. In case of an overdose, if someone has serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. To prevent spreading hepatitis B to others, practice safer sex by using effective barrier methods such as latex condoms or dental dams during sexual activity. Do not share needles. Laboratory and medical tests (e.g., kidney and liver function, HIV tests) may be conducted while you are taking this medication. Keep all lab and medical appointments during and for several months after treatment.
